chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Ash'ari, from Samakah ibn Mihran, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Exalted, did not send any Prophet or Imam except that he is the most knowledgeable of the people regarding Allah's affairs.'

He said: 'And He does not command them except with what Allah commands them, nor forbids them except with what Allah forbids them, nor do they assume authority over any matter except by Allah's command, nor do they look at each other except by His permission, nor do they speak except with what Allah teaches them.'
He said: 'If they lie about Allah and His Messenger, then they are the most unjust of people.'
ai.seo_question: What is the basis for the knowledge and authority of the Prophets and Imams in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this hadith to anchor the Shia doctrine of *Ismah* (infallibility), arguing that the Prophets and Imams are divinely protected from error in both conveying revelation (*tabligh*) and interpreting divine law (*ta'wil*). This establishes their authority as the sole, unerring interpreters of the Quran, ensuring the continuity of divine guidance after the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
